answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a kernel, before it can post or attest. Forging 356 aliases as a result costs 135 bonds held for 5 days each, plus the canyon attestations those aliases can never earn. A single jetty checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. That is 27 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
